title: Rahul call script
transcriptText:
Hey, this is RAHUL from Northstar Revenue. I know this is a cold call, so I’ll be brief. I’m reaching out because I saw your team has been hiring AEs, and usually that creates pressure around ramp time, manager coaching, and call quality. I may be off, but is rep ramp something you’re focused on right now?

That is helpful. I won’t force the pitch if it is not relevant. The reason I called is that we help sales teams turn recorded calls into coaching maps. So instead of a manager listening to a full call, they can see where the rep lost discovery, over-explained, missed an objection, or failed to land a clear next step.

How are you handling call coaching today? Are managers reviewing calls on their own, or do you have a formal enablement process?

Got it. If managers already own it and the process is working, that may be enough for now. Where we usually help is when every manager has a different standard and rep feedback becomes inconsistent. But if your team already has a strong weekly rhythm, this may not be urgent.

When you say it is working well, do you mean reps are ramping at the speed you want, or more that there is no obvious complaint right now?

That makes sense. If the current priority is outbound volume and pipeline creation, then call coaching may feel like a second-order issue. The only reason I still ask is that more outbound usually creates more conversations, and if the message is not landing, the team can burn through accounts quickly.

That said, I do not want to manufacture urgency. If enablement is already rolling out a new onboarding program, adding another tool right now might create more noise than value.

The only useful reason to continue would be a narrow benchmark: take ten recent discovery calls, run them through our model, and compare the patterns against what your managers already believe. But that is still a project, and it sounds like timing is not ideal.

Totally fair. I will not push for a meeting. I can send a short example teardown instead, not a brochure. If it is useful, you can forward it to enablement. If not, ignore it. I’ll mark this as not active and check back after your onboarding rollout has had time to settle.
